parsed.explanation: Article 489 is used in practice against gender expression, with wide police discretion, arbitrary arrests and publicised names. Article 498 moral charges and gender-expression discrepancies are documented as de facto criminalisation of trans people. Police conduct includes a 2019 handcuffing, filming and online posting of a cross-dresser's ID (state-linked outing with asylum flight), and a November 2024 genital-display allegation that is unconfirmed. Official hostility, a religious authority opposing transition, blocked LGBTIQ organisations, and high violence risk for public LGBTIQ identification are all documented. Remedies are thin: no anti-discrimination law, and only one 2022 assault with arrests. Enforcement frequency is not established for trans people, and no border or facility rule is documented, so this is not organised sweeps at the severe tier. Visitor exposure is still high through police discretion and document checks, placing it in the high-risk band.
